title: Network and server monitoring with Nagios Core for an IT operations centre
challenge: The university's IT operations centre needed continuous visibility of its network and servers, availability tracking against service-level agreements (SLAs), and a quick way to get problems to the people who fix them.
actions: Deployed and configured Nagios Core (open source) to monitor the university's network devices and servers. Configured the Nagios web interface so the monitoring dashboard is published for operations staff, and built alert notifications to Telegram. Keep device configuration, inventory and monitoring data up to date, and prepare regular availability reports on key information systems for management.
result: Staff in charge receive alerts on Telegram as problems occur, making it easier to coordinate and assign work to network and Wi-Fi technicians, and management gets regular availability reporting against SLAs.

title: Endpoint and network security monitoring
challenge: The university needs to detect threats on its endpoints and across its network before they become incidents.
actions: Monitor endpoint security with Sangfor Endpoint Secure, and network security with Sangfor Cyber Command and Stealth Threat Analytics. Provide first-level troubleshooting for network and server incidents.

title: Web Application Firewall operations (FortiWeb)
challenge: The university's public web applications are protected by a Web Application Firewall (WAF), which needs trained cover whenever the primary administrator is unavailable.
actions: Completed FortiWeb Administrator Training and act as backup to the primary administrator, covering and monitoring the university’s FortiWeb WAF.

title: Privileged Access Management proof of concept and load balancer installation
challenge: The IT department evaluated Privileged Access Management (PAM) to secure administrative access, and installed a load balancer to improve the availability of university systems.
actions: Took part in the PAM proof of concept (PoC). Provided standby support during the vendor's installation of the load balancer.

title: Personal academic website for a PhD applicant
challenge: A researcher preparing PhD applications needed a professional online presence to present her research and profile.
actions: Built the site with AI-assisted development (Claude), with sections for About, Research, Education, Activities, an Etsy shop, Q&A and Contact, in Malay and English. Deployed it on GitHub Pages with a custom domain and Cloudflare DNS, and continue to make changes when the client needs them.
result: The client now has her own site to promote herself for PhD applications, at no hosting cost.
